# Burnly v0.1.5

macOS preview release.

## Highlights

- Adds unsigned macOS `.dmg` preview installers for Apple Silicon and Intel.
- Adds signed macOS updater archives so the Settings tab can update macOS
  installs after the first manual `.dmg` install.
- Keeps Linux AppImage and Windows x64 release/update behavior unchanged.
- Documents the macOS Gatekeeper quarantine step for the unsigned MVP preview.

## Install

### Linux

Run:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/fikrilal/burnly/releases/latest/download/install-linux.sh | sh
```

For a pinned install of this release:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/fikrilal/burnly/releases/download/v0.1.5/install-linux.sh | BURNLY_VERSION=v0.1.5 sh
```

### Windows Preview

Download the Windows x64 installer from this release:

```text
burnly-v0.1.5-windows-x86_64.exe
```

The Windows preview installer is unsigned for the MVP. Windows may show an
unknown publisher or SmartScreen warning. Only download Burnly from the official
GitHub release.

### macOS Preview

Download the `.dmg` for your CPU architecture from this release:

```text
burnly-v0.1.5-macos-aarch64.dmg
burnly-v0.1.5-macos-x86_64.dmg
```

Open the `.dmg`, drag `Burnly.app` to Applications, then clear Gatekeeper
quarantine once if macOS blocks the unsigned preview build:

```bash
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Burnly.app
```

## Updates

In-app updates are available from the Settings tab on Linux, Windows, and macOS.
On macOS, the `.dmg` is only the first-install artifact; updates use the signed
`.app.tar.gz` updater archive from the release.

## Verification

Release artifacts include `SHA256SUMS`. Updater metadata is published as
`latest.json`; `latest-linux.json` is kept as a compatibility alias for older
Linux builds.

## Notes

- macOS support is preview.
- macOS Apple Developer ID signing and notarization are deferred until funding
  is available.
- Windows installer code signing is deferred; Tauri updater artifact signing is
  still required.
